verification.note: Unit 5 (Surface Chemistry) is sourced from the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", book pp.76-79, which prints the question and a model answer. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board's, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. The printed question reads "What are colloidal solution?" and is kept verbatim. BOOK ERROR (book p.77, VSAQ 11): the printed answer gives the particle size as "10⁻⁹ to 10⁻⁸" with NO UNIT AT ALL, and with an upper limit that is wrong by two orders of magnitude even when metres are assumed. The NCERT range is 1 nm to 1000 nm, that is 10⁻⁹ m to 10⁻⁶ m, and that range is written on this card. Recording the printed version here rather than following it, because a student who writes 10⁻⁸ as the upper limit excludes most of the sols named in the rest of the chapter. BOOK GAP: the printed answer gives no other property, so the two tests a student is expected to know, passing through filter paper but not through a semi-permeable membrane, and showing the Tyndall effect, are added.

steps.why: The colloidal state is defined by size alone, not by the substance, so the number range is the answer. Below 1 nm the system is a true solution and above 1000 nm it is a suspension, which is why both limits have to be written.
common_mistakes: Writing the size with no unit. A bare 10⁻⁹ to 10⁻⁶ means nothing until metres are written after it.
Giving only the lower limit. Both limits are needed, because the upper one separates a colloid from a suspension.
steps.memory_tip: 1 nm to 1000 nm. Below it a true solution, above it a suspension.
steps.margin_note: Write the range with the unit. A size range without metres or nanometres is usually not given the mark.

steps.label: How a colloid is recognised

lines.text: A colloid shows the Tyndall effect.

lines: filter paper, but they do not pass through
The particles show Brownian movement and
Ex: milk, blood, gold sol, starch sol.
steps.why: The size range cannot be seen, so the answer is completed by the properties that follow from it. Each property is a test in the laboratory: the membrane test separates a colloid from a true solution, the filter paper test separates it from a suspension, and the Tyndall effect can be seen with the eye.
common_mistakes: Writing that colloidal particles are held back by filter paper. They pass through it; only a suspension is held back.
Writing that a colloidal solution settles on standing. It does not, because of Brownian movement and the charge on the particles.
steps.memory_tip: Through filter paper, not through a membrane. That pair of answers fixes the size in the middle.
steps.margin_note: One property plus one example is enough for this mark. The Tyndall effect is the safest one to write.

insider_note: The size range with its unit is the marked line, and the book prints it without a unit and with the wrong upper limit. Write 1 nm to 1000 nm, or 10⁻⁹ m to 10⁻⁶ m.
